Aloof

/ə-LOOF/ — rhymes with roof · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is aloof keeps an emotional distance from others and acts cool or uninvolved instead of friendly.

The new student seemed aloof, reading alone instead of joining the games.

Worked Example

At the reunion, Marcus sat in the corner with his arms crossed, barely greeting anyone and clearly making it known he didn't want to join in.

Aloof is more precise than 'quiet' or 'shy' because it describes a deliberate emotional distance and a cool demeanor—someone who actively keeps others at arm's length through their manner, not just someone who is introverted.

How Aloof Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

cold

cold: showing little warmth or friendly feeling

reserved

reserved: quiet and slow to share feelings

withdrawn

withdrawn: pulled back from contact with others

Antonyms

friendly

friendly: warm and pleasant toward other people

approachable

approachable: easy to talk to and welcoming

How Strong Is It? — sociable → reserved → distant → aloof

sociable vs. aloof

sociable vs. aloof: Sociable sits at the opposite end of the scale from aloof: a sociable person seeks out company, while an aloof person deliberately keeps others at arm's length.

reserved vs. aloof

reserved vs. aloof: Reserved is milder than aloof — a reserved person is simply quiet and slow to open up, but an aloof person adds a cool, standoffish air that discourages others from approaching.

distant vs. aloof

distant vs. aloof: Distant comes close to aloof but is a shade weaker: a distant person seems far away in the moment, while aloof suggests a settled, deliberate coolness toward others.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — a-

Prefix — a-: on, toward (Old English (an))

Root — loof

Root — loof: the windward side of a ship, steered toward to keep clear of danger (Dutch (loef))

Put it together

Put it together: Aloof began as a sailor's command: keep the ship a- ('toward') the loof, the windward side, to stay safely clear of a dangerous shore. That picture of deliberately steering clear survives in today's meaning — an aloof person keeps an emotional distance, staying apart instead of drawing near.

Use the root in a new word: luff

Use the root in a new word: luff: Sailors still luff a boat by turning it toward the wind — the same windward idea hidden inside aloof, which first meant keeping a ship safely at a distance.

Word Choice

informal to formal

Reach for aloof when someone deliberately keeps emotional distance through their manner and demeanor. It's stronger and more intentional than 'quiet' or 'shy.' Use it when the cool distance is noticeable and seems deliberate, not just a side effect of nervousness.
